1402:
** δουλ-όω**,
**enslave,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.27; δουλοῖς καὶ σὲ καὶ πᾶσαν πόλιν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 254, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 467; δ. φρόνημα 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.61}}:—mostly in _passive_, **to be enslaved,** ὑπὸ Πέρσῃσι, ὑπὸ Ἁρπάγου, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.94, 174, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.98}}; αἱ ψυχαὶ δεδούλωνται {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 23; δεδουλωμένοι τῇ γνώμῃ, τὴν γνώμην ἐδουλοῦντο, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.34, 7.71; ἐλεύθερος πᾶς ἑνὶ δεδούλωται, νόμῳ 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 699, cf “Sam.” 280}}:—_middle_ (with _perfect_ δεδουλῶσθαι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.82)}}, **make subject to oneself, enslave,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] 1.18, 5.29, 7.68, 75, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Menexenus” 239d; τὸν ἥσσονα δουλούμεθ᾽ ἄνδρα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 493; ἐπιθυμίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 838d; τὸ ἑαυτοῦ θειότατον ὑπὸ τῷ ἀθεωτάτῳ.. δουλοῦται [prev. author] “R.” 589e.}}

** δῠνάστ-ης**, ου, ὁ,

1417:
** δύο** [ῠ],
also **δύω** in _Epic dialect_, Eleg. and late, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“SIG” 1231 (Nicomedia, 3rd-4th c.AD), not in _Ionic dialect_ Inscrr. nor in Trag. (δύο ῥοπάς should be read in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1090)}}, nor in _Attic dialect_ Prose or Inscrr.: _Laconian dialect_ _accusative_ δύε {{Refs|“IG” 5(1).1; Thess. _feminine_ δύας [prev. work]9(2).517}}: _genitive_ and _dative_ δυοῖν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ διαίτης” 1.3, but _falsa lectio_ in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11, 91 [used as monosyllabic in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 640, compare δώδεκα for δυώδ}}-]; later _Attic dialect_ also δυεῖν (especially in _feminine_ _genitive_) found in codices of {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 536, cited from 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus by 2nd c.AD: Aelius Dionysius Grammaticus (?) “fragment” 372, compare 1.20 (codex Laur.)}}; _Boeotian dialect_ δουῖν {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.54; later δυσί, δυσὶν ἡμέραις 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.101 codices, δυσὶν ἡμέρῃσι variant in 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Acut.(Sp.”) 67; δυοῖν ὄμμασι καὶ δυσὶν ἀκοαῖς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1287b27, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 699, “SIG” 344.26 (Teos, 4th c.BC)}}, etc.: early _Attic dialect_ Inscrr. have δυοῖν {{Refs|“IG” 12.3.10, +others, later δυεῖν “SIG” 2587.286, “IG” 22.463.78, +others, from 3rd C on δυσί [prev. work]1028.27, +others}}; _Ionic dialect_ _genitive_ δυῶν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“GDI” 5653d9 (from Chios), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.94, 130, etc., _dative_ δυοῖσι [prev. work] 32, 7.104}}; δυῶν also _Doric dialect_, {{Refs|“Leg.Gort.” 1.40, “Tab.Heracl.” 1.139; δυοῖς “Leg.Gort.” 7.46.}}— Used _indeclinable_, like{ἄμφω}, by {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (who has no _genitive_ or _dative_ δυοῖν), τῶν δύο μοιράων 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.253; δύω κανόνεσσι 13.407, etc.; so in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus}} and _Attic dialect_, δύο νεῶν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.82; δύο ζεύγεσι [prev. author] 3.130; δύο νεῶν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.89; δύο πλέθρων 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.9}}; with dual, δύο μναῖν uncertain reading {{Refs|[prev. author] “Mem.” 2.5.2}}; but not in Trag. and rare in Comedy texts, ἔτεσιν δύο {{Refs 4th c.BC+|2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 105; δύ᾽ ἔτεσιν 4th-3rd c.BC: Damoxenus Comicus 2.3}}: not in _Attic dialect_ Inscrr. before the Roman period, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|“IG” 3.1443, +others:—two, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.16, etc.; in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, δύο and δύω}} are sometimes joined with plural Nouns, δύο δ᾽ ἄνδρες {{Refs|18.498, +others}}; also in Trag., δύο κριούς {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 237 (Lyric poetry)}}; in _Attic dialect_ Prose, δύο τέχνας {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 464b}}; but δυοῖν is rare with plural Nouns, ὀρθοστάταις δυοῖν {{Refs|“IG” 2.1054.64}}; ἕνα καὶ δύο one or **two**, a few, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.346; δύ᾽ ἢ τρεῖς 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 829, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.20}}; εἰς δύο **two and two**, {{Refs|[prev. author] “Cyr.” 7.5.17}}; σὺν δύο **two** together, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.224, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.66}}; δύο ποιεῖν τὴν πόλιν to split the state into **two**, divide it, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1310a4.}}
1418:
** δῠσ-**,
insepar. Prefix, opposed to εὖ, **un-, mis**-, with notion of **hard, bad, unlucky**, etc., as δυσήλιος, δύσαγνος; **destroying the good sense** of a word, or **increasing its bad sense**: hence, joined even to words expressing negation, as δυσάμμορος, δυσανάσχετο; _poetry_ in strong contrasts, as Πάρις Δύσπαρις, γάμος δύσγαμος. Before στ, σθ, σπ, σφ, σχ, the final ς was omitted, see δυστ-. (Cf. Sanskrit _du[snull]-, dur_-, e.g. **durmanās**, ={δυσμενής}; ONorse **tor**-, e.g. **torsóttligr** (δύσμαχος); OIr. **du-, do**-, e.g. **dochruth** 'misshapen'.)

Latin _suesco_; see at {βεσόν}.)
1486:
** ἔθω**,
**to be accustomed, to be wont**: _present_ only in _participle_, κακὰ πόλλ᾽ ἕρδεσκεν ἔθων much ill he wrought **after his wont**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.540; οὓς παῖδες ἐριδμαίνωσιν ἔθοντες 16.260 (in these passages some Grammars explained ἔθων}} as, ={βλάπτων},{φθείρων} (and it was so used by {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 108), and (in 16.260) ἐρεθίζων, compare ἔθει· φθείρει, ἐρεθίζει, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, ἐθρίς, ἴθρις)}}: _perfect_ εἴωθα {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.766, etc.}}, _Epic dialect_ and _Ionic dialect_ ἔωθα {{Refs|8.408, etc.}}, is used as _present_; _pluperfect_ εἰώθειν, _Ionic dialect_ ἐώθεα, as _imperfect_; _participle_ εἰωθώς, _Ionic dialect_ ἐωθώς, also in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Archippus Comicus 48, Araros 19}}; _Doric dialect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_ _perfect_ ἐθώκατι {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus}}: mostly with _infinitive_, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.766, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.31, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.99, etc.: _impersonal_, ὡς εἴωθε}} as **is the custom**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 282; ὥσπερ εἰώθει 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sulla” 9, etc.}}: frequently _absolutely_ in _participle_, of persons, **accustomed, customary, usual**, ἡνιόχῳ εἰωθότι {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 5.231}}; ὑμῖν.. τοῖς εἰώθοσιν **who are used** [to hear me], {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 939}}; οὐκ ἐωθώς **praeter morem**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.111}}; of things, τὰ ἐωθότα νοήματα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] 3.80; ἐν τῷ εἰ. τρόπῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 27b, etc.: frequently in _neuter_, παρὰ τὸ εἰ}}. contrary to **custom**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.17, 55}}; τὰ εἰ. **ordinary things**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51, etc.}}
